Resource 0 · Before you start

Getting Started With Claude

What this guide covers

This is a practical, step by step guide to getting Claude set up on your devices. It covers where Claude is available right now, how to install it in each app.

For guidance on what you should and should not put into Claude, see the AI Use Handbook. This guide sits alongside it and covers the how, not the how to use it well.

Where you can use Claude today

WhereAvailable nowNotes
Claude OnlineYesGood start point / what you will be use to interacting with.
Claude Desktop appYesRecommended “home” interface where you interact with claude.
Connects to your approved work files (via local connections, so you have to have your files sync’d down from Sharepoint)
Claude mobile appYesHandy for quick questions on the go. No access to your work files, but the history from claude on your computer exchanges will be there.
Claude in ChromeYesBrowser extension, opens as a side panel
Claude for Excel, Word and PowerPointYesOne install adds Claude to all three apps
Claude for Outlook / connection to other M365 platformsNot yetWaiting on our Microsoft 365 connection.

Before you start: getting your Claude account

You need to be added to our Claude Team account before any of the steps below will work.

  1. Request access using the AI tool request form, found in the AI Integration Teams channel.
  2. Wait for approval. Once your request is approved, you will be added to the DQ / LWT Claude Team account.
  3. From there, you can sign in wherever you see Claude, using your DQ / LWT work email.

Setting up Claude Desktop

Claude Desktop is Claude's own app for your computer, separate from your browser or Office apps. It is well suited to longer pieces of work, and it can read files you choose to share with it.

  1. Go to claude.com/download and choose the version for your computer, Mac or Windows.
  2. Open the downloaded file and follow the installer prompts.
  3. Open Claude Desktop and sign in with your DQ / LWT work email.

Setting up the Claude mobile app

The Claude mobile app is useful for quick questions, dictating notes, or picking up a conversation you started on your computer. It cannot open your work files, so keep it to general work rather than anything drawn from member, financial, or HR information.

  1. Open the App Store on iPhone or iPad, or Google Play on Android, and search for Claude by Anthropic.
  2. Install the app and open it.
  3. Sign in with your DQ / LWT work email, using the same sign in method you use elsewhere.
  4. If your phone is set up with work security policies, follow any prompts from IT to confirm the app is allowed.

Setting up Claude in Chrome

Claude in Chrome adds Claude as a side panel in your browser. It can read what is on a webpage and help with research, summarising, or filling in forms, with your say so at each step.

  1. Open Chrome and go to the Chrome Web Store listing for Claude.
  2. Select Add to Chrome, then confirm.
  3. Click the Claude icon in your browser toolbar and sign in with your DQ / LWT work email.
  4. Open the side panel whenever you want Claude's help on a page. It will not run in the background unless you open it.

Setting up Claude for Excel, Word and PowerPoint

This is one install that adds a Claude side panel to Excel, Word and PowerPoint at the same time. You only need to do this once, on each device you use.

  1. Go to the Claude for Microsoft 365 listing on Microsoft AppSource.
  2. Select Get it now to install.
  3. Open Excel, Word or PowerPoint. On Windows, find Claude under Home, Add-ins. On Mac, find it under Tools, Add-ins.
  4. Sign in with your DQ / LWT work email.

Why isn't Claude in Outlook yet?

Claude for Outlook exists as a product, but connecting it needs to go through our Microsoft 365 environment, and that connection is not set up yet.

This is part of our wider IT and governance work, not something specific to Claude. Once it is ready, we will add setup steps to this guide and let the team know.

If you get stuck

For any questions about access, installation, or anything that is not working as expected, get in touch with Eilidh directly.

Resource 1 · Get comfortable

Claude basics 101

An introduction guide for DQ / LWT staff
1

Introduction: What is Claude?

Claude is more than a chatbot. It's a family of AI models, modes and tools you can use to research, write, plan, analyse and build things, in plain conversation.

  • Think of Claude as a capable assistant you talk to like a colleague, not a search engine.
  • It comes in different modes for different jobs (Chat, Cowork, Code, Design) and different models with different strengths.
2

Getting Set Up

This guide covers how to use Claude well day to day. For installing apps and getting access, see the DQLWT Claude Setup Guide.

Setting your personal preferences

Claude lets you save context about how you work, so every response is tailored without you repeating yourself.

  1. Open Claude and go to Settings.
  2. Find Personal Preferences (sometimes called Custom Instructions).
  3. Add a short note on your role, the tone you prefer, and any formatting habits (e.g. "keep responses brief", "I work in tourism data and stakeholder comms").

Recommended to use the “Know me” tool to generate your custom instructions

You can look at and adjust any other preference etc in settings as well to have clause set up in a way that works for you.

3

Learning to Prompt Claude

Prompting is the highest-leverage skill to learn first. Communicating clearly is the difference between an average result and a great one.

The core idea: treat Claude like a capable new colleague who simply lacks your context.

Three habits to build early

  • Be specific about the output format you expect (e.g. "a table", "three bullet points", "a short email").
  • Give Claude the reasoning behind the request, not just the task.
  • Use examples wherever you can.
4

Understanding the Models

The model picker controls which "version" of Claude you're using. Each is suited to different tasks - more advanced models cost more and run slower. You can also select effort as well, and toggle on and off thinking (for more / less complex tasks).

ModelBest forTrade-off
FableMost advanced - complex builds and reasoningSlower, most expensive
OpusStrong coding and agentic tasksStill relatively costly
Sonnet (recommended default)Strong all-rounder for everyday workBalanced speed, cost, quality
HaikuFast, simple, high-volume tasksLess depth on complex tasks

Model names and numbers change over time - models will update frequently and this table will be out of date quickly, so check what the latest models are suitable for).

5

7

Context Windows and Tokens

  • Context window = how much information Claude can "hold in mind" at once - like short-term memory.
  • Tokens = the bite-sized pieces text, images and documents get broken into so Claude can process them.
  • Rough scale: bigger models (e.g. opus) handle around 1 million tokens (~750,000 words); smaller models (e.g Haiku) handle around 200,000.
  • Practical takeaway: long documents, images and long conversations all eat into that limit - start a new conversation for a new topic.
6

Artifacts

  • You will start seeing “Artifacts” in Claude as you work.
  • Artifacts are interactive outputs Claude creates while you are working with it.
  • They can include documents, code snippets, visual previews, or small web apps you can view inside Claude.
  • They let you preview the output in the same workspace, then keep chatting with Claude to make changes and see the result update.
  • Do not worry if they pop up while you are learning. They are just another way Claude shows and stores work in progress.
8

Your First Claude Interaction

Pick a real, small pain point from your own role. Some starting ideas: summarising a report, drafting an itinerary, cleaning up a spreadsheet, drafting a stakeholder email.

  1. Write a clear first prompt
  2. Review Claude's output.
  3. Refine your prompt and repeat until you're happy with the result.

Note: "interaction" here just means a task idea - not the Claude Projects feature.

9

Resource 2 · Go further

Claude intermediate 102

How to learn Claude: intermediate concepts for DQ / LWT staff

By now you should be comfortable with the basics: getting set up, prompting, models, modes, and your first project. This is where Claude stops being "a useful chatbot" and starts becoming a customised assistant that works the way you do.

1

Understand Agents (cowork environment)

An AI agent perceives its environment, works out what it needs, and makes decisions to reach a goal, rather than just answering one question at a time.

  • The key difference from a standard chatbot: an agent decides which tools or integrations it needs, then calls on them itself to carry out a plan.
  • Claude Cowork is DQ / LWT's outcome-driven agent - it can run multi-step workflows across the files, folders and apps on your computer, not just chat back and forth.
  • You still stay in control: Cowork proposes its plan and checks in with you before doing anything irreversible.

More about cowork
https://anthropic.skilljar.com/introduction-to-claude-cowork

2

Build With Artifacts

In the beginner guide, artifacts appeared automatically when Claude decided one was the best format. The next step is asking for one on purpose.

  1. Describe the outcome you want (a one-pager, an itinerary, a small dashboard, a checklist, an HTML page, a word doc, a powerpoint, an excel file) rather than just the content.
  2. Ask Claude to build it as an artifact so it opens in its own panel next to the chat.
  3. Keep chatting to refine it - layout, wording, colours - and watch it update live.

More about Artifacts
https://claude.com/resources/tutorials/intro-to-artifacts

3

Customise Claude: System Prompts, Projects and Skills

Claude's default answers follow a generic pattern because of its system prompts - Anthropic's own "master instructions" that set Claude's baseline identity and guardrails on claude.ai and the mobile apps. Understanding this is what opens the door to a more personalised Claude.

Projects

  • A Project lets you set custom instructions - context, tone, output preferences - that apply to every conversation inside it, similar to your own mini system prompt.
  • You can also attach reference files (a style guide, past reports, key data) as Project knowledge, so Claude always has that context on hand without you re-uploading it each time.

Prompt to help set up Project instructions

More about setting up projects:
https://claude.com/resources/tutorials/intro-to-projects
https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9519177-how-can-i-create-and-manage-projects

Skill files

  • Skills are modules with step-by-step instructions for a specific outcome - useful for templates or tone-of-voice rules Claude should follow every time.
  • Skills will be built and issued centrally by DQ / LWT. Don't install or use skill files from anywhere other than DQ / LWT or Anthropic directly.
  • To call a skill backslash /

This matches Anthropic's own guidance: use Skills only from trusted sources, since a skill can direct Claude to run code, access data, or make external requests - treat installing one like installing software.

More about skills:
https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512176-what-are-skills
https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512180-use-skills-in-claude
https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512198-how-to-create-custom-skills

4

Plugins: Extend Claude Safely

Right now we won’t be using plugins (as of August 2026).

Plugins bundle skills, connectors and automations together into a single install, so you get a ready-made set of capabilities in one go instead of assembling them yourself.

  1. Only install plugins that come from DQ / LWT or directly from Anthropic.
  2. Don't install community or third-party plugins on your own, even if they look useful.
  3. If you spot a plugin you think would help, flag it to the AI Integration Team rather than installing it yourself.

Why: a plugin can bundle skills and connectors that run code, reach your files, or call external services. Anthropic's own security guidance treats plugin and skill installation like installing software - only ever from a source you trust.

5

Research: Going Deeper

Claude's default knowledge has a training cut-off, so it can miss recent developments. Research closes that gap by searching and reasoning agentically instead of answering from memory alone.

  • When switched on, Claude runs a chain of linked searches, using each result to decide what to check next.
  • It explores a question from multiple angles automatically, and returns an answer with citations you can check yourself.
  • Good uses: current events, market or competitor checks, verifying a stat before it goes in a report.

More about using research: https://claude.com/resources/tutorials/using-research

6

Connectors: Bringing In Your Data

Connectors (built on a standard called MCP) let Claude reach into other systems directly - Google Drive, Slack, SharePoint - instead of relying only on files you upload by hand.

  • Once a connector is authorised, you can ask things like "summarise last week's updates in this Slack channel" or "find the latest version of this file in Drive", and Claude pulls it in live.
  • Connectors are third-party integrations, not Anthropic products - only connect ones DQ / LWT has approved, and only using our official DQ / LWT accounts, never a personal login.
  • Never connect a service that would give Claude access to member, financial or HR data unless DQ / LWT has specifically approved that connector for that purpose.

More information on connectors: https://claude.com/resources/tutorials/connect-your-tools-to-unlock-a-smarter-more-capable-ai-companion

7

Sharing and Collaboration

A chat, Project or artifact doesn't have to live in one person's account. Sharing means a teammate can pick up exactly where you left off, instead of starting from scratch.

  • Open the conversation, Project or artifact and use Share.
  • Choose whether the other person can just view it, or continue the conversation themselves.
  • Send them the link - within a shared Project, everyone sees the same custom instructions and knowledge files, so the team works from one source of truth.
8

Cowork Task Loops and Automations

The beginner guide covered Cowork for one-off requests. It can also handle recurring or multi-step work that keeps running without you re-prompting at every stage.

  1. Describe the outcome and how often it should happen (e.g. "every Monday morning").
  2. Let Cowork propose the steps it will take.
  3. Review and approve the plan before it runs unattended.
  4. Check progress and results via the task list as it works.

Good candidates: a weekly report pulled from the same folder, or a bulk clean-up across a large batch of files.
